Least-privilege, read-only steps verified against the provider's documentation.

Close
Cloudflare
Read-only zone and ruleset polling
ACCESS MODE
CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Zone list, then the rulesets attached to each zone.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
Zone > Zone > Read. Add Zone > WAF > Read to include rulesets.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
The token string, or {"api_token":"..."}
Steps
In the Cloudflare dashboard open My Profile > API Tokens and select Create Token.
Choose Create custom token and give it a recognizable name.
Add the permission Zone > Zone > Read, and optionally Zone > WAF > Read.
Under Zone Resources, limit the token to the zones you want validated.
Select Continue to summary, then Create Token, and paste the token here once.
Never performed

Never edits DNS records, rules, or zone settings.

Troubleshooting

If the poll reports a rulesets permission gap, the token lacks Zone > WAF > Read. Zones still import; rulesets are skipped.

Least-privilege, read-only steps verified against the provider's documentation.

Akamai EdgeDNS
Read-only zone polling
ACCESS MODE
CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Edge DNS zone list and the record sets in each zone.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
API service "DNS—Zone Record Management" at READ-ONLY access.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
{"host":"...luna.akamaiapis.net","access_token":"...","client_token":"...","client_secret":"..."}
Steps
In Akamai Control Center open Identity and Access Management and create an API client.
Use the advanced option so you can choose individual APIs and access levels.
Grant only DNS—Zone Record Management with READ-ONLY access.
Download the credential and copy host, access_token, client_token and client_secret.
Paste the four values as JSON here once.
Never performed

Never creates, changes, or deletes zones or record sets.

Troubleshooting

A 401 usually means the host does not match the credential set. A 403 means the client lacks the DNS API grant.

Least-privilege, read-only steps verified against the provider's documentation.

Close
GoDaddy
Read-only domain polling
ACCESS MODE
CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Domain list for the account (Domains v1 list endpoint).
MINIMUM PERMISSION
Production API key and secret. GoDaddy keys are not scoped, so AstraNull only calls the domain list endpoint.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
{"key":"...","secret":"..."}
Steps
Sign in to the GoDaddy developer portal with the account that holds the domains.
Create an API key for the Production environment, not OTE.
Copy the key and secret immediately; the secret is shown once.
Paste them as JSON here once.
Never performed

Never changes DNS records, contacts, renewals, or purchases.

Troubleshooting

A 403 means the account has no domains or no plan with domain API access. GoDaddy has scheduled key and secret auth for deprecation on Domains APIs; personal access tokens are not yet supported here.

Least-privilege, read-only steps verified against the provider's documentation.

Close
Namecheap
Read-only domain polling
ACCESS MODE
CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Domain list via namecheap.domains.getList.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
Namecheap API access with one allowlisted IPv4 egress address. Keys are not scoped, so AstraNull only calls getList.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
{"api_username":"...","api_key":"...","client_ip":"203.0.113.10","environment":"production"}
Steps
Confirm eligibility: 20 or more domains, or the account balance or two-year spend threshold Namecheap lists.
Open Profile > Tools > Business & Dev Tools > Namecheap API Access and turn API access on.
Add the AstraNull egress IPv4 address to the whitelist. Ask your operator for it.
Copy the API key. The API username is your Namecheap account username.
Paste the JSON here once, using the same allowlisted address as client_ip.
Never performed

Never registers, renews, transfers, or edits domains or host records.

Troubleshooting

An invalid IP error means client_ip is not on the whitelist or differs from the real egress address. Only IPv4 addresses can be whitelisted.

CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Zone list for the account.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
DNS permission "View zones" only. Leave "Manage zones" off.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
The API key string, or {"api_key":"..."}
Steps
In IBM NS1 Connect open User Settings > Users & teams and select the API keys tab.
Select Create API key and name it for AstraNull.
Under DNS permissions enable View zones only, and clear every other permission.
Save, copy the key, and paste it here once.
Never performed

Never creates or changes zones, records, monitors, or filter chains.

Troubleshooting

A 401 means the key was revoked or mistyped. A 403 means the key does not have View zones.

AWS WAF setup guide

Least-privilege, read-only steps verified against the provider's documentation.

Close
AWS WAF
Read-only web ACL polling
ACCESS MODE
CREDENTIAL POLLING
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
AWS WAF web ACLs (ListWebACLs, GetWebACL). Route 53 zones are not polled; record them as manual metadata.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
IAM policy allowing wafv2:ListWebACLs and wafv2:GetWebACL. The broader managed policy AWSWAFReadOnlyAccess also works.
CREDENTIAL FORMAT
{"access_key_id":"...","secret_access_key":"...","region":"us-east-1","session_token":"optional"}
Steps
In IAM create a customer managed policy that allows only wafv2:ListWebACLs and wafv2:GetWebACL.
Attach it to a dedicated IAM user or role used only by AstraNull.
Create an access key, or issue temporary credentials with a session_token.
Paste the JSON here once. Under Advanced metadata pick Regional or CloudFront scope.
Never performed

Never creates, updates, or associates web ACLs, rule groups, or IP sets.

Troubleshooting

CloudFront web ACLs only list from us-east-1; AstraNull forces that region when CloudFront scope is selected. AccessDenied means the policy is missing one of the two actions.

Google Cloud DNS
Manual metadata
ACCESS MODE
MANUAL METADATA
WHAT ASTRANULL READS
Nothing. You record selected zone metadata as a normalized snapshot.
MINIMUM PERMISSION
No credential is accepted. Whoever exports the metadata needs only DNS Reader (roles/dns.reader) in Google Cloud.
Steps
Create a Manual metadata connector for Google Cloud DNS.
Export the zone names and hostnames you want validated from your own Cloud DNS project.
Add a manual snapshot with a display ref, resource hash, and config hash. Do not paste raw provider payloads.
Never performed

Never contacts Google Cloud or asks for project access.

Troubleshooting

If a snapshot is rejected, check that display ref, resource hash and config hash are all filled in.

AMP-001 · Open-recursive DNS reflection/amplification

Reflection-Amplification · DNS

Close
Intended detection goal

Intent only: assess validation evidence relevant to A recursive resolver answers arbitrary Internet clients over UDP and does not apply source validation, cookies, or effective response-rate controls.. This is not an observed or detected result.

What failure means

Resolver must not answer recursion for external names when closed.

Control that should prevent it

Close open recursion, response-rate limiting, DNS Cookies where supported, anti-spoofing/BCP38, anycast authoritative service, upstream scrubbing.

Evidence boundary

E3 · SEMANTIC-SAFE EVIDENCE

A bounded check can evaluate the stated behavior. Its run evidence still applies to the check, not automatically to every mapped vector.

How the exposure works

Small spoofed DNS queries are sent to open recursive resolvers with the victim as source. The resolver sends larger replies to the victim, often with EDNS0, DNSSEC, TXT, ANY-like, or otherwise large records.

Defensive indicators

Large unsolicited DNS responses; many resolver source IPs; response traffic without matching outbound queries; fragments may appear.

Scope boundary

Amplification varies greatly by query, record set, EDNS size, DNSSEC, truncation, and fragmentation.
